newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran says 30,000 Iraqi Kurd refugees return home.
newsitem.headline: Iran says 30,000 Iraqi Kurd refugees return home.

text.p: Some 30,000 Iraqi Kurdish refugees sheltering in cold mountain camps in Iran have returned to northern Iraq, a local Iranian official said on Wednesday.
Qassem Hassannejad, head of the Red Crescent relief organisation in northwestern Sardasht, told the Iranian news agency IRNA that refugee camps in the region were almost empty now.
The refugees fled fighting between rival Kurdish factions in northern Iraq that erupted in late August. A recent U.S.-brokered truce has been holding in the region.
Iran said on Tuesday another 8,000 refugees had returned to northern Iraq from camps in Baneh, south of Sardasht.
It was not clear if the figures included some of the 48,000 Iran said last week had gone back to Iraq, leaving 27,000 still sheltering in tent camps in below-freezing temperatures.
United Nations sources in Iraq said last week 55,000 refugees had returned from Iran.
The U.N. refugee agency has asked Iran to move the refugees to warmer regions in the country.
Tehran last week blamed the U.N. agency for delays in providing winter housing for the refugees, accusing it of failing to provide $10 million needed for prefabricated houses.
